evidence.description: The supplied PDF labels itself as the online appendix and gives the paper title and a historical-welfare subsection heading.
evidence.quote:
By What Criteria Do We Evaluate Accounting?
                 Some Thoughts on Economic Welfare and the Archival Literature
                                                   ONLINE APPENDIX
                       The Contribution of Accounting to Welfare Over the Ages

evidence.description: The appendix describes historical accounting examples in prose.
evidence.quote:
Notable evidence of accounting over the course of history includes the following: 1
       The earliest acknowledged forms of accounting emerged in Ancient Egypt, where bookkeepers
        kept meticulous commercial and taxation records. These included (Mohamed, 2019, 325): “tax
        records, agendas, grain distribution tables, accounting tables, distribution records of wages and
        receivables, food orders, materials, lists of various items and materials, lists of the contents of the
        temples, documents for the transfer and delivery of materials and yields”.

evidence.description: The appendix closes with a prose claim about accounting and aggregate welfare.
evidence.quote:
It is difficult to imagine a costly economic activity like accounting flourishing for thousands of years,
and in so many civilizations, without mattering – in the terminology of economics, without contributing
substantially to aggregate welfare.
